name: Acid Bass
description: One-voice bass line synthesizer: a sawtooth or a square through a resonant three-pole low-pass that every note opens and closes, with accents that bite and slides between held keys, for squelching lines and, slowed down, long filtered tones.

params.name: Wave
params.description: The oscillator's shape. Saw is bright and buzzing, with every harmonic; Square is hollow and woody, with only the odd ones.

params.name: Cutoff
params.description: Where the filter rests between notes. Lower is darker and rounder; each note opens it above this point and lets it fall back.

params.name: Resonance
params.description: A ringing peak at the filter's edge. A little adds a nasal vowel, a lot makes each note squelch and whistle as the filter moves. The low end stays.

params.name: Env Mod
params.description: How far each struck note opens the filter above Cutoff before it closes again. None leaves the tone where Cutoff put it.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How long the filter takes to close after a note is struck, from a quick blip to a tone that darkens slowly while it is held.

params.name: Accent
params.description: How much hard-played notes stand out: louder, opening the filter further and snapping shut fast. Several in a row open further each time.

params.name: Slide
params.description: How long the pitch takes to bend to a key pressed while another is still held. Such a note comes back to full loudness but does not open the filter again; keys played apart start on pitch.

params.name: Sustain
params.description: How long a held note takes to fade away. Short makes plucks whatever the key does; at the very top a note holds until the key is let go. A key tied over a fading note starts the fade again.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Distortion after the filter. Clean at the bottom and only a little thicker over the first quarter; by half way dark sounds have grown a buzzing edge and bright ones are squashed and a little brighter. Further up adds more of the same, less and less. The level stays about the same.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it catches peaks at high settings.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit; no circuit, schematic, recording or sample was used. It is built from general knowledge of how one-voice bass line synthesizers of this kind are made: one oscillator switched between a sawtooth and a square, a low-pass of three poles with resonance, separate loudness and filter envelopes, accented steps and slides between tied notes. Choices of this device, not measurements of an original: the three poles are equal trapezoidal stages in one loop (a real filter of this kind has unequal stages), tuned down as resonance rises so the peak stays on Cutoff; 60 % of the passband level the loop takes is given back; five octaves of envelope sweep; an accent adds up to 6 dB with velocity, opens the filter one octave further on the strike, shortens the filter's fall towards 0.2 s and charges a store (150 ms in, 350 ms out) worth up to four octaves; the slide covers 99 % of the interval in its time; a 2 ms strike, an 8 ms rise back to full loudness for a tied key and a 3.5 ms release time constant; Drive is a saturator after the filter and before the loudness envelope, following a square-root law above its knee rather than a hard limit so that its level can be made up for any patch, with up to 36 dB of gain that follows the control as d(2 - d), so that the lower half of its travel is heard; four times oversampling; a 2 Hz DC blocker; no keyboard tracking of the filter. A key pressed over a held one slides, brings the loudness back to full and starts its fall again, but does not strike the filter envelope or charge an accent; when the held note has faded to complete silence it strikes as a fresh note does. Tuned by measurement only: nobody has listened to it.
